ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, a rectangular sheet of paper $ABCD$ is folded along $EF$, such that vertices $C$ and $D$ respectively fall on points $C'$ and $D'$. The line $CE$ intersects $AF$ at point $G$, and $\angle CEF = 70^\circ$. What is the value of $\angle GFD'$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD \parallel BC$,\\
it follows that $\angle DFE + \angle CEF = 180^\circ$, $\angle AFE = \angle CEF$,\\
given that $\angle CEF = 70^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle DFE = 180^\circ - \angle CEF = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$, $\angle AFE = 70^\circ$,\\
From the fold, it is known that: $\angle D'FE = \angle DFE = 110^\circ$, therefore $\angle GFD' = \angle D'FE - \angle AFE = 110^\circ - 70^\circ = \boxed{40^\circ}$;

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A rectangular sheet of paper $ABCD$ is folded along $EF$, such that vertices $C$ and $D$ respectively fall on points $C'$ and $D'$. The line $CE$ intersects $AF$ at point $G$, and $\angle CEF = 70^\circ$. What is the value of $\angle GFD'$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Since $AD \parallel BC$, it follows that $\angle DFE + \angle CEF = 180^\circ$ and $\angle AFE = \angle CEF$. Therefore, $\angle GFD' = \angle D'FE - \angle AFE = 110^\circ - 70^\circ = \boxed{40^\circ}$.
